payload.as_is:
PAIN 1 - a close produces nothing. shipMerge runs a plain git merge of the iteration branch, and if nothing was ever committed to that branch it merges an empty branch, reports merged:true, and creates no commit at all. Witness: i8c-phone-connect, 2026-07-24 - the process completed all ten gates and marked itself shipped while trunk's HEAD never moved and 45 files sat uncommitted; the owner discovered it the next morning.

PAIN 2 - nothing commits during an iteration. There is no lane that commits at a milestone, so the branch stays empty until a close that never writes to it. All work lives as uncommitted files in one working directory. Witness: the same run - iter/i8c-phone-connect sat at its fork point for the whole iteration, and the entire deliverable existed only as dirty files.

PAIN 3 - work can be destroyed by tidying up. Because nothing is committed, removing a worktree deletes content permanently. Witness: this session, during Step 0 - i8c's four acceptance tests existed ONLY inside the worktree; a routine worktree removal would have destroyed them, and they survived only because a file-by-file comparison was run first.

PAIN 4 - trunk collects the record it was never meant to hold. A merge brings the whole branch tree, so evidence, gate records and dead machine state land on trunk beside the live claims. Witness: commit 1389fe5 in this repo - 72 files, of which about 57 are evidence documents that the design says must stay on the branch.

PAIN 5 - the record has no named handle. Nothing tags an iteration at close, so once its events are only at a branch tip they are findable by branch name at best, and by raw hash if the branch is ever cleaned up. Witness: se-v2-design §4 states the tag is load-bearing for exactly this reason; no code creates one.

PAIN 6 - a fresh worktree cannot verify itself. It carries no node_modules, so npm run verify fails at tsc before a single test runs, and it forks from whatever was committed at the time, so it can run a stale engine against current tests. Witness: i8c's build gate, where the first battery failed with "tsc is not recognized" and the second failed because the worktree predated the i5c engine fixes; both are logged as se.raid-worktree-provisioning-incomplete.
